- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

content.text:
All clear. Here's what I found and fixed.

## Root cause

The Pause/Suspend buttons looked like they did nothing because of an **RLS permissions mismatch**:

- **Edit** works because it goes through `/api/farmer/update-listing`, which uses the Supabase **service-role** key and bypasses RLS.
- **Delete** works because there's an explicit anon DELETE policy (`produce-listings-delete-policy.sql`).
- **Pause/Suspend** were calling the **anon** Supabase client's `.update()` directly. There is **no UPDATE RLS policy** on `produce_listings`, so PostgREST matched **0 rows and returned no error**. The UI flipped optimistically, then the background reload reverted it — and the database never changed. So consumers kept seeing and could keep ordering the produce.

The display filters themselves were already correct (consumer browse, search, region, and the public profile tab all filter to `status === 'available'`) — they just never had anything to hide because the status was never persisted.

## Changes (`src/app/farmer/dashboard/page.tsx`)

All three status toggles now route through the same service-role API that Edit uses:
- `handleToggleListingSuspend` (inline dashboard list)
- `handleTogglePause` and `handleToggleSuspend` (Manage Listings modal) — refactored through a shared `setListingStatus` helper, with proper error surfacing and re-sync on failure.

## Defense-in-depth (`src/app/api/orders/place/route.ts`)

Order placement previously fetched listings by ID with **no status check**, so a stale cart could still order a paused/suspended item. Now it rejects any listing whose status isn't `available` ("… is no longer available."). This also covers moderator-suspended produce.

Typecheck passes (`tsc --noEmit`).

One thing worth knowing: this fix works because `/api/farmer/update-listing` runs with the service-role key and verifies ownership via the signed farmer cookie — the proper long-term fix is still to add a real UPDATE RLS policy on `produce_listings`, but routing through the API matches the existing pattern and unblocks you now.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-1000/bundled-skills/2.1.181/b3fd76c20a65ca51fc1e5234121ca87f/verify

**Verification is runtime observation.** You build the app, run it,
drive it to where the changed code executes, and capture what you
see. That capture is your evidence. Nothing else is.

**Don't run tests. Don't typecheck.** Running them here proves you
can run CI — not that the change works. Not as a warm-up,
not "just to be sure," not as a regression sweep after. The time
goes to running the app instead.

**Don't import-and-call.** `import { foo } from './src/...'` then
`console.log(foo(x))` is a unit test you wrote. The function did what
the function does — you knew that from reading it. The app never ran.
Whatever calls `foo` in the real codebase ends at a CLI, a socket, or
a window. Go there.

## Find the change

The scope is what you're verifying — usually a diff, sometimes just
"does X work." In a git repo, establish the full range (a branch may
be many commits, or the change may still be uncommitted):

```bash
git log --oneline @{u}..              # count commits (if upstream set)
git diff @{u}.. --stat                # full range, not HEAD~1
git diff origin/HEAD... --stat        # no upstream: committed vs base
git diff HEAD --stat                  # uncommitted: working tree vs HEAD
gh pr diff                            # if in a PR context
```

State the commit count. Large diff truncating? Redirect to a file
then Read it. Repo but no diff from any of these → say so, stop.
**No repo → the scope is whatever the user named; ask if they
didn't.**

**The diff is ground truth. Any description is a claim about it.**
Read both. If they disagree, that's a finding.

## Surface

The surface is where a user — human or programmatic — meets the
change. That's where you observe.

| Change reaches | Surface | You |
|---|---|---|
| CLI / TUI | terminal | type the command, capture the pane — [example](examples/cli.md) |
| Server / API | socket | send the request, capture the response — [example](examples/server.md) |
| GUI | pixels | drive it under xvfb/Playwright, screenshot |
| Library | package boundary | sample code through the public export — `import pkg`, not `import ./src/...` |
| Prompt / agent config | the agent | run the agent, capture its behavior |
| CI workflow | Actions | dispatch it, read the run |

**Internal function? Not a surface.** Something in the repo calls it
and that caller ends at one of the rows above. Follow it there. A
bash security gate's surface isn't the function's return value — it's
the CLI prompting or auto-allowing when you type the command.

**No runtime surface at all** — docs-only, type declarations with no
emit, build config that produces no behavioral diff — report
**SKIP — no runtime surface: (reason).** Don't run tests to fill
the space.

**Tests in the diff are the author's evidence, not a surface.** CI
runs them. You'd be re-running CI. Tests-only PR → SKIP, one line.
Mixed src+tests → verify the src, ignore the test files. Reading a
test to learn what to check is fine — it's a spec. But then go run
the app. Checking that assertions match source is code review.

## Get a handle

**Check `.claude/skills/` first — even if you already know how to
build and run.** A matching `verifier-*` skill is the repo's
evidence-capture protocol: it wraps the session so a reviewer can
replay what you saw (recording, screenshots). Drive the surface
without it and you get a verdict with no replay.

```bash
ls .claude/skills/
```

- **`verifier-*` matching your surface** (CLI verifier for a CLI
  change, etc.) → invoke it with the Skill tool and follow its
  setup. Mismatched surface → skip that one, try the next. Stale
  verifier (fails on mechanics unrelated to the change) → ask the
  user whether to patch it; don't FAIL the change for verifier rot.
- **`run-*` but no matching verifier** → use its build/launch
  primitives as your handle.
- **Neither** → cold start from README/package.json/Makefile. Timebox
  ~15min. Stuck → BLOCKED with exactly where, plus a filled-in
  `/run-skill-generator` prompt. Got through → note the working
  build/launch recipe so it can become a `verifier-*` skill.

## Drive it

Smallest path that makes the changed code execute:

- Changed a flag? Run with it.
- Changed a handler? Hit that route.
- Changed error handling? Trigger the error.
- Changed an internal function? Find the CLI command / request / render
  that reaches it. Run that.

**Read your plan back before running.** If every step is build /
typecheck / run test file — you've planned a CI rerun, not a
verification. Find a step that reaches the surface or report BLOCKED.

**The verdict is table stakes. Your observations are the signal.**
A PASS with three sharp "hey, I noticed…" lines is worth more than a
bare PASS. You're the only reviewer who actually *ran* the thing —
anything that made you pause, work around, or go "huh" is information
the author doesn't have. Don't filter for "is this a bug." Filter for
"would I mention this if they were sitting next to me."

**End-to-end, through the real interface.** Pieces passing in
isolation doesn't mean the flow works — seams are where bugs hide.
If users click buttons, test by clicking buttons, not by curling the
API underneath.

**Destructive path?** If the change touches code that deletes,
publishes, sends, or writes outside the workspace and there's no
dry-run or safe target, don't drive it live. Verify what you can
around it and say which path you didn't exercise and why.

## Push on it

The claim checked out — that's the first half. Confirming is step
one, not the job. The description is what the author intended;
your value is what they didn't.

You know exactly what changed. Probe *around* it, at the same
surface you just drove:

- **New flag / option** → empty value, passed twice, combined with a
  conflicting flag, typo'd (does the error name it?)
- **New handler / route** → wrong method, malformed body, missing
  required field, oversized payload
- **Changed error path** → the adjacent errors it didn't touch —
  did the refactor catch them too, or only the one in the diff?
- **Interactive / TUI** → Ctrl-C mid-op, resize the pane, paste
  garbage, rapid-fire the key, Esc at the wrong moment
- **State / persistence** → do it twice, do it with stale state
  underneath, do it in two sessions at once
- **Wander** → what's adjacent? What looked off while you were
  confirming? Go back to it.

These aren't a checklist — pick the ones the change points at. Stop
when you've covered the obvious adjacents or hit something worth a
⚠️. A probe that finds nothing is still a step: "🔍 passed `--from ''`
→ clean `error: --from requires a value`, exit 2." That the author
didn't test it is exactly why it's worth knowing it holds.

Still not a test run. You're at the surface, typing what a user
would type wrong.

Stdout, response bodies, screenshots, pane dumps. Captured output is
evidence; your memory isn't. Something unexpected? Don't route around
it — capture, note, decide if it's the change or the environment.
Unrelated breakage is a finding, not noise.

Shared process state (tmux, ports, lockfiles) — isolate. `tmux -L
name`, bind `:0`, `mktemp -d`. You share a namespace with your host.

## Report

Inline, final message:

```
## Verification: <one-line what changed>

**Verdict:** PASS | FAIL | BLOCKED | SKIP

**Claim:** <what it's supposed to do — your read of the diff and/or
the stated claim; note any mismatch>

**Method:** <how you got a handle — which verifier/run-skill, or
cold start; what you launched>

### Steps

Each step is one thing you did to the **running app** and what it
showed. Build/install/checkout are setup, not steps. Test runs and
typecheck don't belong here — they're CI's output.

1. ✅/❌/⚠️/🔍 <what you did to the running app> → <what you observed>
   <evidence: the app's own output — pane capture, response body,
   screenshot>

🔍 marks a probe — a step off the claim's happy path, trying to
break it. At least one. A Steps list that's all ✅ and no 🔍 is a
happy-path replay: still PASS, but you stopped at the first half.

**Screenshot / sample:** <the one frame a reviewer looks at to see
the feature — an image for GUI/TUI, code block for library/API;
omit for build/types-only>

### Findings
<Things you noticed. Not just bugs — friction, surprises, anything
a first-time user would trip on. "Took three tries to find the right
flag." "Error message on typo was unhelpful." "Default seems odd for
the common case." "Works, but slower than I expected." Lower the bar:
if it made you pause, it goes here. But the pause has to be yours,
from running the app — not from reading the PR page. A red CI check,
a review comment, someone else's bot: visible to anyone already, and
you relaying it isn't an observation. Claim/diff mismatch, pre-existing
breakage, and env notes also belong.

Each probe gets a line here even when it held — "🔍 empty `--from`
→ clean error" tells the author what *was* covered, which they
can't see from a bare PASS.

sticking out is itself rare.>
```

**Evidence has to reach the reader.** A file path is only evidence
if the person reading the report can open it. If the `SendUserFile`
tool is in your toolset, you're on a remote surface where they
can't — send the screenshots and recordings with it and let the
report name what you sent. Without it, reference the path and keep
the evidence that matters inline — pane captures and response
bodies travel in the report; a bare path only works when the reader
shares your filesystem.

**Verdicts:**
- **PASS** — you ran the app, the change did what it should at its
  surface. Not: tests pass, builds clean, code looks right.
- **FAIL** — you ran it and it doesn't. Or it breaks something else.
  Or claim and diff disagree materially.
- **BLOCKED** — couldn't reach a state where the change is observable.
  Build broke, env missing a dep, handle wouldn't come up. Not a
  verdict on the change. Say exactly where it stopped +
  `/run-skill-generator` prompt.
- **SKIP** — no runtime surface exists. Docs-only, types-only,
  tests-only. Nothing went wrong; there's just nothing here to run.
  One line why.

No partial pass. "3 of 4 passed" is FAIL until 4 passes or is
explained away.

**When in doubt, FAIL.** False PASS ships broken code; false FAIL
costs one more human look. Ambiguous output is FAIL with the raw

DB restored cleanly (`available`, stock 84). Here's the verification report.

## Verification: farmer Pause/Suspend take-down of produce

**Verdict: FAIL** — the code change is correct and necessary, but **suspend still won't work in production until a DB migration is applied**. Testing surfaced a second, deeper blocker that my code fix alone doesn't resolve. I've written the migration; it must be run in the Supabase SQL editor.

**Claim:** When a farmer taps Pause/Suspend, the status must persist so consumers can no longer see or order the produce.

**Method:** Cold start (no skills). Ran `npm run dev` (Next 16, localhost:3000). Minted a valid `yff_farmer` HMAC cookie from `SESSION_SECRET`, drove the real HTTP routes against the live Supabase, and read the DB back via the REST API with the service-role key. Tested on the real "Green leaf" listing (the one from your screenshot); restored it after.

### Steps
1. ✅ **Reproduced the original bug** — anon-client `PATCH produce_listings` → HTTP **200, `rows: []`**, DB stayed `available`. The silent 0-row no-op under RLS is exactly why the buttons appeared to do nothing.
2. ❌ 🔍 **My fix exposed a hidden blocker** — suspend via the new service-role API path → HTTP **500**: `violates check constraint "produce_listings_status_check"`. The DB **rejects** the values `paused` and `suspended_by_farmer`.
3. 🔍 **Mapped the constraint** (against the real row, restored after): `available, coming_soon, sold_out, suspended` → ALLOWED; **`paused`, `suspended_by_farmer` → REJECTED (23514)**. The farmer take-down statuses were never valid at the DB level.
4. ✅ **Mechanism works once status is valid** — used `coming_soon` (an allowed status) as a proxy: API take-down → HTTP 200, DB persisted, and listing **disappeared from `/api/produce`** (consumer can't see it).
5. ✅ **Order guard works** — guest order for the taken-down listing → HTTP **400 "Green leaf is no longer available."**, and `stock_qty` stayed 84 (guard fires before any stock claim). Restored to `available`.

**Sample (the decisive captures):**
```
1. ANON update -> http 200 rows: []                 | DB: available   (silent no-op = the bug)
2. API suspend -> http 500 ...produce_listings_status_check violated  (constraint blocks it)
   paused -> REJECTED 23514 ; suspended_by_farmer -> REJECTED 23514
4. API takedown(coming_soon) -> 200 | in /api/produce: false          (consumer hidden ✅)
5. order(taken down) -> 400 {"Green leaf is no longer available."}     (order blocked ✅, stock untouched)
```

### Findings
- ⚠️ **Blocker — migration required.** `scripts/produce-status-farmer-takedown-migration.sql` (written) extends the CHECK constraint to allow `paused` and `suspended_by_farmer`. **It is not yet applied** — I can't run DDL through the REST API. Until you run it in the Supabase SQL editor, clicking Suspend will now show a 500 error instead of silently failing. The code fix + migration are a package; ship them together.
- ⚠️ **The display side was already correct all along.** Once status actually persists, `/api/produce`, search, region, and the profile tab all hide non-`available` produce — verified live in step 4. The whole bug was that the write never landed (RLS no-op + invalid status value).
- The order-placement guard is well-placed: it rejects before stock is claimed, so a stale cart can't oversell or order a taken-down item. Also covers moderator-`suspended`.
- 🔍 Confirmed the constraint only fires on rows that actually match — my first constraint probe (against a non-existent id) misleadingly showed everything "allowed"; re-running against the real row gave the true result above.

Want me to also confirm the migration once you've run it (I can re-test `paused`/`suspended_by_farmer` directly), and then commit both files? I won't push without your go-ahead.

content.text:
Yes — exactly one. The code fix alone won't work until you run this in Supabase, because the database currently **rejects** the `paused` and `suspended_by_farmer` status values. I already saved it to `scripts/produce-status-farmer-takedown-migration.sql`.

**Supabase Dashboard → SQL Editor → New query → paste → Run:**

```sql
ALTER TABLE produce_listings
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS produce_listings_status_check;

ALTER TABLE produce_listings
  ADD CONSTRAINT produce_listings_status_check
  CHECK (status IN (
    'available',
    'coming_soon',
    'sold_out',
    'pending_review',
    'rejected',
    'suspended',           -- moderator take-down
    'suspended_by_farmer', -- farmer Suspend button
    'paused'               -- farmer Pause button
  ));
```

What it does: drops the old check constraint and recreates it with `paused` and `suspended_by_farmer` added (it keeps all the existing allowed values, so nothing else breaks). It's safe to run on live data — your current rows are all `available`/`coming_soon`/etc., which stay valid.

After you run it, tell me and I'll re-test the real `paused`/`suspended_by_farmer` values end-to-end (right now I could only verify the mechanism using `coming_soon` as a proxy). Then I'll commit both the code and the migration — and ask before pushing.

I checked the code, and here's what I found: **this feature is already fully built and wired end-to-end.** Here's my understanding of your request mapped to what already exists:

**1. Reason while suspending (moderator side)** — ✅ exists
`src/app/moderator/consumers/page.tsx` prompts the moderator for a reason when they hit Suspend, and it's **mandatory** (blocks if empty):
> "Reason for suspending {name}? సస్పెండ్ చేయడానికి కారణం? (e.g. Multiple fake orders)"

It's sent to `PATCH /api/moderator/consumers/[id]`, which saves it to the `consumers_auth.suspended_reason` column (I confirmed that column **exists** in your Supabase). Reactivating clears it.

**2. Shown in the consumer header, highlighted** — ✅ exists
`src/components/consumer/GlobalNav.tsx` renders a **red banner** (🚫, `bg-red-600`) at the top:
> **ACCOUNT SUSPENDED / ఖాతా నిలిపివేయబడింది**
> _{the moderator's reason}_

It's driven by `suspendedReason` from `ConsumerAuthContext`, fed by `/api/consumer/me`, and cached in `localStorage` so it survives the session being cleared.

---

So the code for exactly what you described is already there. One nuance worth knowing: a suspended consumer is **blocked at login** (`/api/consumer/login` rejects them with the reason in the error message), so the **header banner** mainly shows for someone who gets suspended *mid-session*. A freshly-suspended person logging in sees the error message, not the header banner.

Given that the last two features you reported also *looked* done but were actually broken at the DB/RLS layer — **do you want me to verify this one actually works end-to-end** (simulate a suspended consumer and confirm the banner renders)? Or are you seeing it fail / wanting a change to how it behaves (e.g. show the banner even on a blocked login attempt)?

cat > /tmp/wire.py <<'PYEOF'
import re, sys
files = sys.argv[1:]
for path in files:
    s = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    lines = s.split('\n')

    # 1. ensure 'use client'
    if not lines[0].strip().startswith("'use client'") and not lines[0].strip().startswith('"use client"'):
        lines = ["'use client'", ""] + lines

    # 2. add useLang import if missing
    text = '\n'.join(lines)
    if 'useLang' not in text:
        # insert after last top-of-file import line
        last_imp = -1
        for idx, ln in enumerate(lines[:60]):
            if ln.startswith('import '):
                last_imp = idx
        imp = "import { useLang } from '@/lib/LanguageContext'"
        if last_imp >= 0:
            lines.insert(last_imp+1, imp)
        else:
            # after use client (line 0/1)
            ins = 1
            lines.insert(ins, imp); lines.insert(ins, "")

    # 3. insert hook after component body opening brace
    text = '\n'.join(lines)
    if not re.search(r'\{[^}\n]*\bL\b[^}\n]*\}\s*=\s*useLang\(\)', text):
        # find export default function
        start = None
        for idx, ln in enumerate(lines):
            if re.search(r'export default function', ln):
                start = idx; break
        if start is not None:
            depth = 0; seen_paren = False; insert_at = None
            for idx in range(start, len(lines)):
                ln = lines[idx]
                depth += ln.count('(') - ln.count(')')
                if '(' in ln: seen_paren = True
                if seen_paren and depth == 0 and ln.rstrip().endswith('{'):
                    insert_at = idx; break
            if insert_at is not None:
                indent = '  '
                lines.insert(insert_at+1, f"{indent}const {{ L }} = useLang()")
    open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(lines))
    print("wired", path)

input.command:
cd /home/veerendra/farmer/yourfamilyfarmer
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import re, glob
files = set(glob.glob('src/**/*.tsx', recursive=True) + glob.glob('src/**/*.ts', recursive=True))
changed = 0
for path in files:
    s = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read()
    if 'useLang()' not in s: continue
    def repl(m):
        inner = m.group(1)
        names = [x.strip() for x in inner.split(',') if x.strip()]
        if 'L' in names: return m.group(0)
        names.append('L')
        return 'const { ' + ', '.join(names) + ' } = useLang()'
    new = re.sub(r'const \{([^}]*)\} = useLang\(\)', repl, s)
    if new != s:
        open(path,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(new); changed += 1
        print("added L ->", path)
print("files changed:", changed)
PYEOF
echo "=== re-typecheck ==="

content.text: Found the bug: my `body_range` mis-counted braces on multi-line destructured signatures (`}) {`), so it saw empty bodies (e.g., admin's `DeliveryRow`). Let me rewrite the detector to use a span-to-next-component approach (no fragile close-brace matching) and re-run.

input.command:
cd /home/veerendra/farmer/yourfamilyfarmer
cat > /tmp/addhook2.py <<'PYEOF'
import re, sys

START_RE = re.compile(r'^(export\s+)?(default\s+)?function\s+[A-Z]\w*\s*\(|^(export\s+)?const\s+[A-Z]\w*\s*(:[^=]+)?=\s*\(')

def open_idx_of(lines, start):
    depth = 0; seen = False
    for i in range(start, min(start+60, len(lines))):
        depth += lines[i].count('(') - lines[i].count(')')
        if '(' in lines[i]: seen = True
        if seen and depth <= 0 and lines[i].rstrip().endswith('{'):
            return i
    return None

for path in sys.argv[1:]:
    lines = open(path, encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    starts = [i for i,ln in enumerate(lines) if START_RE.search(ln)]
    starts_sorted = sorted(starts)
    inserts = []
    for idx, st in enumerate(starts_sorted):
        o = open_idx_of(lines, st)
        if o is None: continue
        nxt = starts_sorted[idx+1] if idx+1 < len(starts_sorted) else len(lines)
        body = '\n'.join(lines[o:nxt])
        if 'L(' in body and '= useLang()' not in body:
            indent = (re.match(r'\s*', lines[o+1]).group(0) if o+1 < len(lines) else '  ') or '  '
            inserts.append((o, indent))
    for o, indent in sorted(set(inserts), reverse=True):
        lines.insert(o+1, f"{indent}const {{ L }} = useLang()")
    if inserts:
        open(path,'w',encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(lines))
        print(f"{path}: +{len(inserts)} hooks")

input.command:
cd /home/veerendra/farmer/yourfamilyfarmer
cat > /tmp/brmerge.py <<'PYEOF'
import re, glob
TE = 'ఀ-౿'
te_re = re.compile(f'[{TE}]')
def esc(s): return s.replace('\\','\\\\').replace("'", "\\'")
files = glob.glob('src/**/*.tsx', recursive=True)
total=0
for path in files:
    lines = open(path,encoding='utf-8').read().split('\n')
    out=[]; i=0; n=len(lines); changed=False
    while i < n:
        a = lines[i]; at = a.strip()
        m = re.match(r'^([^<>{}]+?)<br ?/?>$', at)
        if m and not te_re.search(at) and i+1 < n:
            b = lines[i+1]; bt = b.strip()
            if te_re.search(bt) and not re.search(r'[<>{}]', bt):
                indent = a[:len(a)-len(a.lstrip())]
                out.append(f"{indent}{{L('{esc(m.group(1).strip())}', '{esc(bt)}')}}")
                i += 2; changed=True; total+=1; continue
        out.append(a); i+=1
    if changed:
        open(path,'w',encoding='utf-8').write('\n'.join(out))
        print("merged in", path)
print("total br-merges:", total)
PYEOF
python3 /tmp/brmerge.py

1	import { Language } from './translations'
2	
3	/**
4	 * Produce names and varieties are stored bilingually as "English / తెలుగు".
5	 * Show only the side that matches the active language. When there's no "/"
6	 * separator we return the whole string unchanged, so single-language values
7	 * (and names that happen to contain no slash) are left alone.
8	 */
9	export function localizeName(value: string | null | undefined, lang: Language): string {
10	  if (!value) return ''
11	  const sepIdx = value.indexOf('/')
12	  if (sepIdx === -1) return value.trim()
13	  const en = value.slice(0, sepIdx).trim()
14	  const te = value.slice(sepIdx + 1).trim()
15	  return lang === 'te' ? te || en : en || te
16	}

The whole-app language separation is complete. Here's the summary. ## What changed **The problem:** the app showed both languages at once in several formats — `"All / అన్నీ"` (slash), English heading + separate Telugu subtitle, `English
Telugu`, and `{en}/{te}` data fields. **The approach:** I used the existing `L(en, te)` helper from `LanguageContext` (which returns one side based on the toggle) and converted every bilingual display site to it. This was a large, verified codemod across **53 files** + 2 new files. **Coverage (all done, build + typecheck clean):** - **488 inline `"English / తెలుగు"`** strings → `L('English', 'తెలుగు')` (JSX text, attributes, JS strings, template literals) - **Separate-element pairs** (heading+subtitle, `
` splits) → merged into single `L()` calls - **Module-scope option/label arrays** (`TYPE_OPTIONS`, `STATUS_LABEL`, `VEHICLE_OPTIONS`, `UNIT_OPTIONS`) → converted to `(L) => [...]` factories so they localize reactively - **Data arrays** (`CATEGORIES`, buyer-protection cards) → rendered with `L(x.en, x.te)` - **`alert`/`confirm`/`prompt`** dialogs → `L()` - **5 API routes** (login, OTP, reset, consumer-login) → `tr(lang, en, te)`, reading a new `yff_lang` **cookie** - Every screen: navbar, tabs, buttons, filters, dropdowns, product cards, cart, complaints, profile, forms, error messages, popups, splash, role gate, 404/error pages, admin/moderator/rider/farmer/consumer areas **Persistence:** already worked via `localStorage` (`yff_lang`); I added a mirrored cookie so server-rendered API errors also respect the choice. Survives refresh and navigation. **Two structural changes worth noting:** - `buyer-protection` was a server component exporting `metadata`; I split it into a server page + `BuyerProtectionContent` client component (build blocker otherwise). - New files: `src/lib/serverLang.ts` (server `reqLang`/`tr` helpers) and `BuyerProtectionContent.tsx`. **Verification:** - `tsc --noEmit`: **0 errors** - `npm run build`: **succeeds**, all routes compile - Runtime smoke test: `/consumer` and other routes return 200; default render is English-only — **no `All / అన్నీ`**, no stray `English / Telugu` anywhere. The only remaining `/` with Telugu is a code comment in `localizeName.ts`. - `localizeName` (DB-stored bilingual produce names) already splits by language — confirmed. One caveat I can't fully automate-verify: I confirmed the **English** default render and the `L()` logic is trivial (`lang === 'te' ? te : en`), but I didn't click the toggle in a real browser to watch Telugu render live. If you want, I can drive it with a headless browser. Otherwise this is ready. Want me to commit and push? (53 modified + 2 new files; on `main`, I'll confirm before pushing.)
